children: Dell Technologies (DELL, Financials) is heading into earnings with traders hoping for anything except a muted reaction.
Shares were down more than 4% Tuesday morning near $436 and the options market is pricing in a move of roughly 11% after the company publishes results after the closing bell.
That is a swing of around $50 in either way per share.
This stance demonstrates how split the traders are.
The $400 put has the most open interest in the chain, with 2,972 contracts, which is a negative. The $440 put also was hopping Tuesday with 1,574 contracts traded.
There is also plenty of upside interest. The $500 strike has the largest open interest on the call side with 2,446 contracts, and the $470 strike has a sizeable cluster as well.
That puts Dell smack in the heart of a rather large post-earnings conflict.
The key question for investors is whether Dell can continue to convert robust demand for AI infrastructure into stronger earnings.
The company has profited from a boom in purchases of AI servers and data centers, but expectations are high and profitability is under pressure.
With options pricing such a big move, Dell's outlook may be as significant as the headline profit figures.
The next question is whether the data provides enough to get the bulls above $500, or forces traders back to the highly contested $400 barrier.

title: Dell Traders Are Bracing for a $50 Earnings Swing
